evidence: app/package.json:8-10 — pins hono 4.13.14, @hono/node-server 2.1.5 and htmx.org 2.0.11, all verified as npm 'latest' today
app/server.mjs:5 — html tagged templates from hono/html, the current non-JSX rendering primitive in Hono 4
app/server.mjs:310 — htmx 2.x attributes (hx-get/hx-target/hx-swap/hx-push-url/hx-trigger) with no legacy htmx 1.x idioms anywhere
app/server.mjs:51-53 — serveStatic from @hono/node-server/serve-static, the current split-package location (hono/<runtime> subpaths are what Hono 5 removes; this import is already the new layout)
app/server.mjs:806-810 — serve({ fetch: app.fetch, port }) is the current node-server startup form
latest_apis.rationale: Every framework and library is at the current stable release, and imports (hono/html, @hono/node-server/serve-static, htmx 2 attributes) are all the current generation; nothing here is scheduled for removal in Hono 5.

evidence: app/lib/api.mjs:34 — native fetch for all upstream calls, no axios/polyfill
app/server.mjs:47-54, 227 — URLSearchParams and URL for query building and URL parsing
app/views/layout.mjs:53 — loading="lazy" + explicit width/height on sprites (native, no JS lazy-loading)
app/public/styles.css:6,201,607-640 — design tokens via CSS custom properties, grid layouts, media queries; :focus-visible at styles.css:29
app/scripts/build.mjs:4-10 — ES modules with top-level await for the build step
app/lib/api.mjs:34 — no AbortController or timeout on upstream fetch; a hung API stalls requests indefinitely
platform.rationale: Platform-first almost everywhere — native fetch/URL/URLSearchParams, CSS custom properties and grid, htmx-driven debounce instead of hand-rolled JS — but the upstream fetch has no AbortSignal/timeout, which is the one place a platform feature is conspicuously missing.

evidence: app/package.json:12-15 — exactly three runtime dependencies, all current and all load-bearing (hono, node adapter, htmx)
app/scripts/build.mjs:8 — htmx self-hosted from node_modules into public/ at build time rather than a CDN script or an extra bundler
app/lib/format.mjs:1-58 — all display logic hand-rolled in ~60 lines; no lodash/date/format dependencies pulled in
app/public/styles.css — hand-written CSS per the spec, no CSS framework or icon font
dependencies.rationale: Minimal, modern, and each dependency is genuinely needed; htmx is vendored locally instead of relying on a CDN, and nothing heavy or redundant was added.

evidence: app/lib/api.mjs:1-133 — all HTTP data access behind one module; only server.mjs and views/layout.mjs import hono, so a Hono 5 upgrade touches two files
app/server.mjs:83,441,666,746 — the alternate-forms rule (id <= 10000) copy-pasted in four places instead of one helper
app/server.mjs:567,599,647,705,796 — identical try/catch NotFoundError → 404 boilerplate in five handlers instead of an app.onError case
app/server.mjs:557-818 — server.mjs is a ~820-line monolith mixing routing, data shaping and view construction for every page
app/lib/api.mjs:64-98 — raw untyped PokeAPI JSON with zero JSDoc/TS annotations project-wide (0 type lines), so response-shape changes surface as runtime breakage
app/server.mjs:70-100 vs 660-685 vs 735-755 — three near-duplicate 'refs → dedupe → sort by id → cards' implementations
churn_resistance.rationale: The layering is good (data access isolated, hono confined to two files, ESM-only so Hono 5's ESM-only requirement is a non-issue), but the file has real maintenance debt: no type information anywhere, and several business rules and error-handling patterns duplicated rather than centralized.

findings.issue: Upstream fetch has no AbortController, timeout or retry; a slow or hung API server makes every request (and the in-flight promise cache in api.mjs:23) hang indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Wrap fetch with AbortSignal.timeout(...) and fail fast with a typed error handled in app.onError.

findings.issue: PokeAPI response shapes are consumed raw with no JSDoc types or TypeScript anywhere in the project (0 typeLines), so field renames or shape drift surface as silent runtime bugs.
findings.suggestion: Add JSDoc @typedef declarations (or convert to .ts) for the handful of entity shapes used (species, pokemon, move, type, generation), at least at the api.mjs boundary.

findings.issue: The alternate-forms rule (id <= 10000) is duplicated in four places (server.mjs:83, 441, 666, 746); a spec change would require finding all of them.
findings.suggestion: Centralize as isDefaultForm(id) / speciesFromRef() helpers in lib/api.mjs.

findings.issue: The identical try/catch NotFoundError → c.html(notFoundPage(), 404) block is repeated in all five content handlers.
findings.suggestion: Handle NotFoundError once in app.onError (it already exists at server.mjs:802) and let handlers throw.

findings.issue: No devDependencies and no test script of the app's own; the only safety net is the external acceptance suite, so future refactors inside app/ have no fast feedback loop.
findings.suggestion: Add a couple of app.request()-based smoke tests (Hono's documented testing pattern) or at least a typecheck/lint dev dependency.

findings.issue: server.mjs is a ~820-line monolith mixing routing, per-page data shaping and view construction (renderPokemonPage, renderMoveTable, etc. all inline).
findings.suggestion: Move per-page view builders into views/ modules mirroring the existing views/layout.mjs split.

findings.issue: Three near-identical 'pokemon refs → filter forms → dedupe by id → sort → cards' pipelines (here for abilities, again at 746 for types, and generically at 70-100).
findings.suggestion: Fold all three into the existing speciesCardsForRefs helper, which already handles dedupe and ordering.

findings.issue: Dual URL-push mechanisms: hx-push-url="true" on the form/select plus the server's HX-Push-Url header for the same request (also 582 with 310).
findings.suggestion: Keep only the response-header mechanism, which also normalizes the URL (e.g. clamped page), and drop the attribute.

findings.issue: Three one-off serveStatic routes hardcoding individual asset filenames; adding an asset requires a route edit.
findings.suggestion: Mount once, e.g. app.use('/assets/*', serveStatic({ root: PUBLIC_DIR })) (or app.use('*', serveStatic({ root: PUBLIC_DIR, path: 'index.html' })) as fallback).

summary: This app is unusually well-aligned with the current stable stack: Hono 4.13.14, @hono/node-server 2.1.5 and htmx.org 2.0.11 are each npm's latest today, imports use the current split-package layout, and all interactivity rides on native platform features (fetch, URLSearchParams, CSS custom properties, htmx attributes) with no hand-written client JS and only three lean dependencies. Its aging risk is maintenance rather than obsolescence: the codebase is entirely untyped against large raw API payloads, one 820-line route file carries copy-pasted business rules (the id <= 10000 rule appears four times, the 404 try/catch five times), and the app ships no tests or dev tooling of its own. A framework upgrade would genuinely touch few files, but a requirements change would ripple through server.mjs repeatedly.
